metadata.case_name: LUK SHU KEUNG v. KWOK CHI SHING

plaintiff.education_level: EMBA (Sun Yat Sen University, completed February 2004)

source: Dr. Chang S. said that Plaintiff probably suffered from head injury, whiplash injury of cervical spine, contusion of lumbar spine, right sacro-iliac joint and contusions of right ankle.
injuries.icd_description: Acute whiplash associated disorder with complaint of neck pain, stiffness or tenderness only

injuries.icd_description: Contusion of lower back or pelvis

injuries.icd_description: Contusion of lower back or pelvis

source: Both agree that the Plaintiff probably had a contusion of right ankle with soft tissue involvement. They also agree that the same had recovered as Mr. Luk no longer had ankle complaints at the interview.
Physical examination showed there was tenderness over the base of the posterior aspect of Plaintiff’s neck and his two shoulders and contusion of head.
injuries.icd_description: Contusion of other or unspecified sites of head

manifestations.description: numbness along the left upper limb
tenderness and pain on movement over his lumbar spine
pain around the right sacro-iliac joint
swelling and tenderness at the lateral aspect of his right ankle and pain on walking
observed to walk slowly with a limp
pain on prolonged standing (over 1 hour), walking (30 minutes) and sitting (2 hours)
slight restriction of lateral rotation of cervical spine

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Could not participate in hobbies such as playing tennis and squash; limited recreational and sports activities.
Limited ability to return to pre-accident job as a project manager; restricted to light jobs with shorter hours and more rest between tasks.
